threads.question: Does the town pay for engineering of the track and turf field, and what would rebuilding them cost?

threads.caveat: This asks the town to borrow for a STUDY of the field, track, drainage and wall — not for the work itself. What the work would cost is not established anywhere here.

of the lower retaining wall at the track is in a state of failure, the superintendent said

history.what: A turf field project was already on the Capital Planning Committee's list at $800,000. The minutes say the town had not set money aside for it, and that it was an FY18 project at the earliest.
quotes: Projects Turf Field: $800,000.
However, the Town has not accrued funds to pay for this.
So this is an FY18 project at the earliest.

history.what: The committee asked whether big projects like renovating the track and field belong in the capital planning process at all. A member favored keeping every capital project in one process; the minutes record no decision. Bond counsel said the field does not qualify for contingency fund spending.
quotes: Whether the Capital Planning Process should include large projects (e.g. building re-use projects, renovation of the turf track and field
Kerry said there was an advantage in having all capital projects irrespective of size or funding mechanism in one functional area.
Bond counsel advises that the Turf track and field does not qualify for contingency fund expenditures.

history.what: "Repairs to Turf Field Retaining Wall" (project LPS20-04) was a line in the schools' ten-year capital list at $90,000. Whether it was ever funded or built is not shown here.
quotes: LPS20-04 Schools Repairs to Turf Field Retaining Wall 90,000

history.what: The same retaining wall line (LPS20-04) was listed again, at $98,000.
quotes: LPS20-04 Schools Repairs to Turf Field Retaining Wall 98,000

history.what: The schools' ten-year outlook included a possible $2,200,000 to upgrade the turf field, walls and concession stand, plus a feasibility study of sunken pavers, leaning fencing and walls, and drainage problems on the track and turf field.
quotes: possibly $2,200,000 for the MS/HS to upgrade the turf field, walls, and concession stand
current conditions show sunken pavers, leaning fencing, leaning walls, and drainage issues on the track and turf field
history.where: Document filed under the 26 Oct 2022 Capital Planning Committee agenda, pages 1-2

history.what: Separately, the FY2024 capital plan carried a $50,000 turf field feasibility study and a $150,000 line for engineered drawings from that study.
quotes: LPS23-03 MS/HS Turf Field Engineered Drawings Derived From Feasibility Study $150,000.00
LPS23-06 MS/HS Turf Field Feasibility Study $50,000.00
history.where: FY2024 Town Manager capital plan presentation, page 27 (study also on the committee's composite ranking, page 1)

history.what: The School Committee was told the study would be paid from federal ARPA funds, with capital funds proposed for surveying.
quotes: Turf field, this yea r we will use ARPA funds to do a feasibility study, proposing thru capital funds for surveying

history.what: The School Committee ranked its capital requests. The turf field design was moved to number 7 of the list, 4 to 1 on a roll call; the FY2025-FY2034 plan presented on 20 November shows it at that rank.
quotes: Mr. Lehtinen makes a motion to move the Middle High school turf field design to #7 and bumps number 8 & 9 respectively
Mr. Lehtinen – yes, Mrs. Brzozoski – yes, Mr. Beardmore – yes, Mr. Sculimbrene – no, Ms. Archambault – yes

history.what: The schools put the field in the FY25-FY34 plan as four phases: a study (paid with ARPA funds), then $200,000 in FY25 for a survey and drainage, $300,000 in FY26 and $1.2 million in FY27. The plan says the turf needs replacing within 3-4 years and may have to close to athletics and the public. The School Committee's ranking of this request is shown as 7.
quotes: The turf will need to be replaced within the next 3-4 years.
Phase I is a feasibility study of the use of the land, priority of needs and estimated costs and has been ARPA funded.
Phase 4 FY27 - $1.2 million
(SC Priority Ranking 7)
history.where: FY25-FY34 schools capital plan, presented 20 Nov 2023, pages 4-6

history.what: The study was awarded to Collins Civil Engineering. A member stressed the timeline, because the field had two, maybe three, years of life left.
quotes: awarded to Collins Civil Engineering
the field has 2 maybe 3 years of life left to it

history.what: The School Committee's number 1 ask on the list it sent to the Select Board was finishing the turf field study.
quotes: The number 1 ask is to have the study on the turf field completed

history.what: The committee heard the field and complex would cost an estimated $920,000 (hardscape and drainage), and $500,000 more to replace the turf and track.
quotes: turf field and complex estimated to cost $ 920,000
It will cost an additional $ 500,000 to replace the turf and track.

history.what: The School Committee and its Capital Planning representative went over the draft capital plan, which included the turf and track.
quotes: to include the turf and track

history.what: A committee member said the Town Manager had told him the track and field project "needs more work and is not really at presentation stage", and that he agreed it could go forward without full scoping. The superintendent answered that the schools kept it in because of its priority.
quotes: she mentioned to me that um the track and field project in particular needs more work and is not really at presentation stage
I agreed that we would go forward without the full scoping of the of the track and field project
We kept it in because of the priority and process
history.where: Capital Planning Committee, 29 Oct 2025, at 46:30 (from the recording)

history.what: The School Committee voted on a revised FY27 capital plan. The superintendent described its FY27 content as the primary school driveway study and playground design. The field was not named in what she said.
quotes: what we have in fiscal year 27 right now is the primary school feasibility study for the entry and driveway expansion and the primary school designer services for playground equipment
history.where: School Committee, 19 Nov 2025, at 52:20 (from the recording)

history.what: On the field, a speaker said it would not all be a capital project, because it would exceed the capital budget, and that it would likely have to be regular borrowing. The captions do not name the speaker or say the field was taken out of the plan.
quotes: the field probably won't all of it won't be a capital project
I think it's going to end up having to be regular borrowing
history.where: School Committee, 19 Nov 2025, at 54:20 (from the recording)

history.what: The same evening the committee was told the field "is not able to be brought forth as part of this capital planning process that we are currently in", being "too complex and too slow", and would likely come as a separate Town Meeting article. The speaker still called it in scope for capital planning, without needing to follow the annual process rigidly.
quotes: it is not able to be brought forth as part of this capital planning process that we are currently in
it's just too complex and too slow
I do think that it is in scope for capital planning
history.where: Capital Planning Committee, 19 Nov 2025, at 9:20 (from the recording)

history.what: The committee discussed not using its inside borrowing source for the track and field, and a possible $2 million borrowing for it.
quotes: with the school track and field that we don't want to necessarily go to that inside borrowing source per se
if we do want to do a $2 million borrowing for a track and field
history.where: Capital Planning Committee, 10 Dec 2025, at 41:10 (from the recording)

history.what: The design proposal came in just under $200,000. The School Committee was told nothing could move forward without the engineering and bid work.
quotes: just under $200,000
we cannot move forward until we have the engineering and bid work

history.what: "Discussion on potential Turf Field Capital Request" was an item on the committee's agenda.
quotes: Discussion on potential Turf Field Capital Request

quotes: the school department obviously did not bring the article uh that had been discussed for uh the engineering plans for the the track and field

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

Whether the water district building is exempt from the proposed stormwater fee
Overhead share of proposed stormwater budget. FinCom flagged the overhead portion of the initial proposed budget as too large and pushed to outsource work to reduce it.

Sewer business manager taking on stormwater billing. Idea floated that the sewer business manager could absorb stormwater billing for a percentage of his salary/time, since he already runs Munis billing four times a year.
UniPay online payment fee. Members looked up their own UniPay transactions to estimate what a per-payment fee would cost the town if used for stormwater billing.

Enterprise fund subsidy for office space/equipment. It was noted the town currently subsidizes enterprise funds for office space and equipment like computers, and stormwater would only owe a fraction of that.

Average single-family home stormwater share. Members each calculated, using different methods (DLS override calculator vs. their own tax-rate math), what an average single-family home currently contributes toward the stormwater line.

Override calculator projection for added funding. Using the Prop 2½ override calculator, members estimated how much an average single-family tax bill would rise if the added stormwater money were structured as an override.
Value of stormwater infrastructure. For public messaging, a member argued the town's stormwater infrastructure is worth roughly as much as the middle-high school, to help residents grasp its scale.

Chapter 90 exclusion from stormwater funding. The group agreed to clarify publicly that the money being requested is not eligible for Chapter 90 reimbursement, since Chapter 90 doesn't cover maintenance.

Sample commercial property contribution (Walmart parcel). A spot-check showed the Walmart-anchored parcel's current tax-based contribution to stormwater versus what a tiered utility fee might collect from it.

UNIL (utility company) contribution comparison. Members compared what the utility company currently pays toward stormwater via property tax against what its share would be if distributed under the new fee.

Line-item budget scenario (town budget vs. utility). A chart compared the current town-budget line for stormwater against a proposed scenario that strips out the engineer/vendor costs, showing the resulting per-resident change either way.

Utility scenario resident vs. commercial burden split. Under a stormwater utility funded by ERUs, the commercial/industrial/other share was estimated to cover a portion of costs, shifting the residential share down from the town-budget scenario.
Weston & Sampson contract precedent. Members noted town meeting had approved paying an engineering firm despite not unanimous support, as a precedent for getting the stormwater bylaw approved.
Sewer bill late fee and minimum charge. Members noted the sewer enterprise fund's late-payment demand-notice fee and its minimum annual charge, as a model for stormwater billing enforcement.

Possible inclusion of stormwater in a town-wide override. The group debated whether to fold stormwater utility funding into a broader Prop 2½ override and what percentage of that override stormwater should represent, worried about it looking disproportionate.
FY26 levy limit and 2.5% increase. A member cited the FY26 levy limit and what a 2.5% override increase would amount to, to gauge how large a stormwater ask would be relative to it.
Salt cost versus plowing cost. It was noted that road salt is nearly as large a winter expense as plowing itself, relevant to whether stormwater-related sand reduction saves real money.

Water district building's exemption from the fee. Members checked the property-use code for the water district building to determine whether it would be billed under the stormwater fee, concluding it is likely a tax-exempt municipal/utility authority.
Commissioners agreed to the Select Board's suggestion of a joint Sewer & Stormwater Commission

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

items.text: Municipal building / Ritter Memorial renovation debt exclusion (Article 34). A debt exclusion to renovate town hall into a meeting house and expand Ritter building for municipal and school offices; residents raised concerns about unknown future operating costs and contingency adequacy.

Marshall Park renovation (Article 28). A debt-exclusion request to renovate Marshall Park; a reduced-scope alternative was also costed out; the parks commission had returned $1.5 million in state grants it could not match in time.

Municipal building design project (Article 29). A debt-exclusion request to renovate the meeting house and Ritter building and build a new town hall, consolidating town and school district offices; the town has spent $937,000 in capital funds over seven years maintaining the current buildings.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.

rule.text: An article gets its own thread when it came up at 3 or more meetings, across at least 2 boards, beyond the routine stops every article gets (the Select Board and the Finance Committee each take it up about 2 times to place it and recommend it); when residents spoke about it or a dispute about it was recorded; or when Town Meeting took up an amendment, postponed it, or divided on it, with at least 15 in 100 on the losing side. Those thresholds are our choice, not the town's.
